title: Implement Optimistic Decode Orchestrator with Model Prioritization and Rollback Paths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need a runtime-level orchestrator that enables an optimistic (speculative) decode path across heterogeneous model variants while minimizing correctness regressions and worst-case latency. Existing attempts focus on single-stage acceptance thresholds or staged fallbacks; this ticket implements an Optimistic Decode Orchestrator (ODO) that prioritizes candidate models, probes with lightweight prefill checks, computes token-level acceptance signals using log-prob and embedding drift heuristics, and supports fast rollback to canonical decode without blocking the request.
design_summary:
ODO components:
- Model Prioritizer: ranks model variants (fast-quantized, mid-tier, canonical) per-request using context features (prompt length, user tier, history tokens, kernel fingerprint).
- Micro-Probe Prefill: for prioritized candidate models, run a trimmed prefill probe (first N KV steps) to capture initial token distributions and KV caches without a full allocation. Probes should be cancellable and lightweight.
- Acceptance Scorer: per-token and per-prefill signals: normalized average log-prob delta vs canonical baseline, top-k entropy, embedding cosine drift between candidate and baseline first-token embeddings, and latency/throughput cost estimate.
- Decision Logic: optimistic-path if acceptance_score >= adaptive_threshold; otherwise fallback. Threshold adapts by traffic tier and observed false-accept rate.
- Non-blocking Fallback: if candidate fails acceptance mid-decode, spawn a background canonical decode continuation that takes over seamlessly (replay KV + tokens) with minimal token duplication for the client.
- Kernel & Attention Awareness: orchestrator exposes kernel compatibility metadata so the prioritizer avoids candidates with known kernel mismatches (e.g., unsupported fused-attention kernels for certain sequence lengths).
- Instrumentation: detailed counters, traces, and sampled token-level logs to compute acceptance ROC and latency deltas.

Key trade-offs: probe cost vs. net token savings; acceptance conservatism reduces cost savings but lowers customer-visible regressions; delayed rollback simplifies correctness but increases tail latency. We favor a conservative initial rollout with canary traffic and aggressive telemetry.
acceptance_criteria:
- ODO must reduce average per-token cost by >=12% on benchmark conversational traces for canary traffic with the fast-tier candidate enabled.
- P95 user-perceived latency must not increase by more than 10ms on canary traffic.
- False-accept rate (cases where optimistic output differs materially per eval set) must be <0.5% on the canonical validation suite.
- Telemetry: traces for every optimistic decision, with sampled token-level logprob/embedding deltas exported to the perf-dashboard.
- Rollback: when acceptance rescinds mid-stream, client-facing continuity must not show duplicated tokens more than once per 10k messages (target duplication <= 0.01%).
- Config: ODO feature flag with per-customer opt-in, and controls for thresholds, probe size, and prioritizer weights via runtime config service.
tasks: Spec: finalize acceptance score formula and adaptive threshold rules
Proto: implement model prioritizer and micro-probe prefill in runtime shim
Telemetry: add token-level logprob and embedding-drift instrumentation (sampling at 1%)
Kernel metadata: extend model catalog schema with kernel capability fingerprints
Fallback: implement non-blocking rollback mechanism with KV replay path
Bench: end-to-end benchmark harness for conversational traces (cost/latency/qa)
Canary: deploy to 5% internal traffic then 10% enterprise canaries
Docs: runbook for rollback and failure modes, plus admin console toggles
measurement_metrics:
- cost_saving_pct (aggregate per-token cost improvement),
- p50/p95/p99 latency delta vs baseline,
- false_accept_rate (evaluation suite),
- rollback_rate and duplication_rate,
- probe_overhead_ms and probe_failure_rate,
- kernel_mismatch_retries
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit tests + microbench harness (2 weeks). Phase 1 (internal canary): 5% internal traffic, full telemetry collection (1 week). Phase 2 (select customers): enable opt-in for 10 enterprise customers, monitor SLOs and false_accept_rate (2 weeks). Phase 3 (gradual ramp): expand to 25% traffic, then 50% if metrics within guardrails. Emergency kill switch in console and auto-disable if false_accept_rate > 0.7% or p95 latency regresses >15ms.
implementation_notes:
- Keep micro-probe CPU/GPU allocations strictly bounded and share GPU buffers where possible.
- Use existing KV cache copy-on-write helpers to avoid full KV duplication for probes.
- Prioritizer should be pluggable: start with static weights, later train a light-weight model with logistic regression.
- Use existing rollout tooling from console to expose per-customer flags and thresholds.
- For embedding-drift compute, use single-step normalized cosine with L2 clipping to avoid outliers.
- Ensure kernel metadata update path is backward compatible; default to conservative route when unknown.
